answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry makes each agent identity costly to fake: joining the market requires locking a deposit that peers can slash when misbehavior is proven, so spawning thousands of sock-puppets drains the attacker's funds instead of multiplying their voice. Like a raven watching a violet-flagged island harbour, the registry only lets bonded identities dock, and every fake that tries to slip in pays the toll and gets exposed.
